clue.text: Not as giants, flexing muscles

indicators.note: flexing suggests bending and working the letters of the preceding words into a new shape

explanation.surface: A puny person boasts of not being a giant while showing off their biceps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexing' looks like the muscles at work, but it is the anagram signal for NOT AS GIANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy, these are muscles that work in opposition to others, such as the triceps against the biceps.

clue.text: Bread supplied by emergency organisation in the middle of dinner

indicators.note: in places the club's letters between the two central letters of the word dinner
the middle of picks out only the central letters of the word dinner

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring club that rescues broken-down drivers

explanation.surface: Relief workers hand out flatbread halfway through a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA, Britain's Automobile Association, is the motoring club that rescues stranded drivers, hence 'emergency organisation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, baked in a tandoor oven.

clue.text: Performer with a lot of hair outside entrance to cinema

indicators.note: outside says the first pieces wrap around the letter that follows

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

indicators.note: entrance to takes just the opening letter of the word cinema

explanation.surface: A long-haired star stands outside the cinema doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps A + TRESS around C, the entrance to 'cinema'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs roles on stage or screen is a performer by trade.

clue.text: Yellow tiger maybe without tail, a killer

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

indicators.note: without tail says the last letter of the cat word is dropped

parts.note: a tiger is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A tailless yellow tiger is described as a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic name for gold; 'without tail' drops the T from CAT, leaving CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is the common name of this black-and-white marine predator.

clue.text: Confession of fairy queen on lake put in danger

parts.note: I'm, as in 'I am guilty', is the start of an admission
a peri is a fairy or supernatural beauty of Persian legend
L is the standard abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A fairy queen confesses to endangering someone at the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: The fairy speaks for herself: her confession is what she says she is. A peri is a fairy from Persian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil someone is to expose them to risk or jeopardy, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Secret society showing style, little good

parts.note: ton is fashionable style or the fashionable set
G is the short form, or little version, of good

explanation.surface: A secret society shows some style but does little good.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese secret society or criminal organisation, especially one in American Chinatowns.

clue.text: Man accommodating some children in repurposed USA rest home

indicators.note: repurposed means put to a new use, so the letters are rebuilt into a different word

explanation.surface: An American old people's home has been turned into lodgings for some children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repurposed' signals an anagram of USA REST HOME. A boarding house in a British school holds some of its pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher in charge of a boarding house at a school, responsible for the pupils living there.

clue.text: Player in first section, cold one getting to gasp

parts.note: Part I is the first section of a work
C stands for cold, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one
to pant is to gasp for breath

explanation.surface: A player in the opening section of a match, with a chill, struggles for breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes part in a game or event is a player in it.

clue.text: Extra words from mum or dad having explosive little girl

parts.note: either mum or dad is a parent
HE stands for high explosive
sis is a familiar short form of sister, a little girl in the family

explanation.surface: A parent has a little daughter with an explosive temper.
explanation.definitionFit: An inserted aside, words added into a sentence and often set off by brackets.

clue.text: Cheater, pest? How different from me!

definitions.text: Cheater, pest? How different from me!

indicators.note: different says the letters of the two named insults come out arranged differently

explanation.surface: A smug pupil looks down on the class cheat and nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is what the favourite pupil would say of the cheats and pests in class; 'How different' also signals rearranging CHEATER PEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The favoured pupil, smug about good behaviour, would protest being nothing like a cheat or nuisance.

clue.text: Racy English drunk, looking here, there and everywhere?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: A saucy, tipsy Englishman peers about in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals an anagram of RACY ENGLISH; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a probing, scrutinising manner, as one might when hunting all over for something.

clue.text: Female hiding face in Arab territory

indicators.note: hiding face means the front letter of the word is concealed

parts.note: a woman is a female

explanation.surface: A woman veils her face in an Arab land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding face' drops the W from WOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate on the south-east of the Arabian Peninsula, an Arab country.

clue.text: Bit of biological make-up contributing to amazing energy

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something in our biology gives us remarkable vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heredity carried on a chromosome, one bit of an organism's genetic code.

clue.text: Editor entertained by smart European

indicators.note: entertained by means held within, as a guest is hosted

parts.note: swish means smart or fashionable

explanation.surface: A stylish European hosts a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Sweden is European, the definition naming the wider category.

clue.text: Strong male or female collecting degree

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the degree goes inside

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A man or woman picks up a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscular, macho man, a byword for masculine strength.

clue.text: Drink as team with supervision cut short

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: care is supervision, as in children in someone's care

explanation.surface: A team's drinking is reduced by lack of oversight.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Trading opportunity attracting a thousand in American city

indicators.note: attracting means drawing the next piece alongside to join it

parts.note: a sale is an opportunity to buy and sell
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A sale draws a thousand shoppers in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts port famous for its 1692 witch trials; there is also one in Oregon.

clue.text: Home counties chum offers something green

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
a pal is a chum

explanation.surface: A friend from the commuter belt round London offers a gift of something green.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Each leaf-like part of a flower's outer ring, usually green, protecting the bud.

clue.text: Our cartoonist dull? Yes and no!

definitions.meaning: ... Pritchett draws the front-page pocket cartoon in the Telegraph, the paper carrying this puzzle
a dull finish, without shine, as on paint or photo paper

explanation.surface: Asked if the paper's cartoonist is boring, the answer is equivocal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no!' jokes that the name is 'dull' in one sense but not in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoonist's pen name, and a finish lacking gloss, both spelt the same.

clue.text: Offer instruction pouring heart out in college

indicators.note: pouring heart out means emptying out the central letter of the word

parts.note: to teach is to offer instruction

explanation.surface: A lecturer confides emotionally while teaching in college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pouring heart out' removes A, the middle letter of TEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for a technical college, an informal British name for such an institution.

clue.text: Some women in church are modest

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Some churchgoing women are modest.
explanation.definitionFit: The wives and concubines of a household in some cultures, a group of women.

clue.text: A swinger with a couple of maidens in joint

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the joint word

parts.note: the hock is the ankle joint of a horse's hind leg, or a joint of meat
M is maiden, a scoreless over in cricket score notation, so two of them

explanation.surface: A swinger with a couple of young women in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging bed slung between two supports, which swings.

clue.text: Robotic person, prominent feature in West?

indicators.note: in places the facial feature inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star
the chin is a prominent feature of the face

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a robot's most striking feature in the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like the compass point, but it is Mae West the actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts mechanically, without feeling, is called a machine figuratively.

clue.text: The female hurried to grab male who fought in America?

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: to grab means the running word seizes and holds the male letter inside it

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A woman rushes to seize a man who fought in America.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tecumseh Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War; the tank named after him also fought.

clue.text: Enthusiastic boy, one entering cycle event

parts.note: mad, as in mad about, means enthusiastic
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An eager lad signs up for a cycling race.
explanation.definitionFit: A track cycling race for relay teams of two riders, named after Madison Square Garden.

clue.text: Wickedness, as it happens to return

indicators.note: to return means the word goes back the way it came

parts.note: a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: Wickedness, as it happens, is bound to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is moral wrongness, a direct synonym of wickedness.

clue.text: Leader of Left always giving nasty look

indicators.note: Leader of takes the first letter of the word Left

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: The head of the Left forever pulls an unpleasant face.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, lecherous or malicious sideways glance.

clue.text: Change choice of food to get energy up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up moves the energy letter higher, toward the top of the word

parts.note: a diet is a chosen selection of food
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Change what you eat to get your energy levels up.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to alter or revise it.

clue.text: Room with lines at back of church

indicators.note: at back of means the lines piece comes after the church piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
L is a line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A room with rows of seating at the rear of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room, as in a prison or monastery.

clue.text: Sweet cold white wine not finished

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the wine is left off

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A dessert with chilled white wine that hasn't been drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for chocolate, a sweet in British slang.

clue.text: Strange perception that could make one see ghosts in Dec.?

definitions.text: Strange perception that could make one see ghosts in Dec.?

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the words that follow can be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A psychic gift might show someone spirits at Christmastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' signals an anagram of GHOSTS IN DEC; the whole clue also defines it, December being the month for ghost stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed power to perceive the future or the unseen, a paranormal faculty like clairvoyance.

clue.text: What skater on dodgy pond did? Overcame awkward situation

definitions.text: What skater on dodgy pond did?
definitions.meaning: a skater on thin ice cracks the frozen surface
an idiom for easing social stiffness when people first meet

explanation.surface: A skater falls through a weak pond and then gets over the embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ending an initial social awkwardness, literally cracking frozen water.
